name: Virginia
summary_text: The July 2026 national legal-risk map places Virginia in its 'Low-Risk' tier — largely refraining from targeting trans adults without extraordinary protection — but it enacted a K-12 facility ban in 2023 (school-focused; limited traveler exposure). Around the national score 0.36.

sources.title: Anti-Trans National Legal Risk Assessment Map: July 2026
sources.claim_summary: Erin Reed's anti-trans national legal-risk assessment map (July 2026 update, via Stonewall News): grades every US state's legislative risk for transgender adults; Idaho entered the top 'Do Not Travel' tier (felony bathroom ban, up to 5 years; the map's fourth such state) and South Carolina rose to 'Worst Laws Passed'; catalogues the nationwide federal rollback (passport and legal-document barriers, funding withdrawals, Pride-crosswalk erasure) and several countries' travel advisories for trans travellers. Places Virginia among 'Low-Risk States (AZ, DE, ME, MI, NV, PA, VA, WI, DC)' and notes Virginia, like Arizona, has enacted anti-trans policies affecting youth that the map's author considers unlikely to be extended to adults.

NOTE: page not retrievable at fetch time (HTTP 404 - the MAP equality-map URL has since moved; the research dossier cites this page for the state-by-state facility-ban list). The underlying source is the Movement Advancement Project equality map of bans on transgender people using public bathrooms and facilities according to their gender identity.
